CLINICAL PROCEDURE NOTE

Patient: Jane Doe
MRN: 11223344
DOB: 05/15/1978
Date of Procedure: 28/01/2026

PROCEDURE: Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy

SURGEON: Dr. Sarah Johnson

INDICATION: 45-year-old female with symptomatic cholelithiasis and recurrent biliary colic.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:
Patient was brought to the operating theatre and placed in supine position. General anesthesia was induced without complications. Abdomen was prepped and draped in sterile fashion.

Four-port laparoscopic approach was utilized. Pneumoperitoneum established with Veress needle. Ports placed at umbilicus (12mm), epigastrium (10mm), and right subcostal region (two 5mm ports).

Gallbladder was identified and appeared inflamed with multiple stones visible. Calot's triangle was carefully dissected. Cystic artery and cystic duct were identified, clipped, and divided. Gallbladder was dissected from liver bed using electrocautery.

Specimen was placed in retrieval bag and removed through umbilical port. Hemostasis was confirmed. Ports were removed under direct visualization. Fascia closed at 12mm port site. Skin closed with subcuticular sutures.

FINDINGS:
- Inflamed gallbladder with multiple stones
- No evidence of bile duct injury
- Liver appeared normal
- No other abnormalities noted

ESTIMATED BLOOD LOSS: 50 mL

COMPLICATIONS: None

SPECIMENS: Gallbladder with stones sent to pathology

CONDITION: Patient tolerated procedure well and transferred to recovery in stable condition.

VITAL SIGNS POST-OP:
- BP: 120/75 mmHg
- HR: 72 bpm
- SpO2: 98% on room air
- Temp: 36.8°C

PLAN:
- Routine post-operative care
- Pain management with oral analgesics
- Diet as tolerated
- Discharge home same day if stable
- Follow-up in 2 weeks

Dr. Sarah Johnson, MD
General Surgery
License: MD12345
